headline: Funding flows. Competition grows. Satellites shrink.
deck: This week highlights funding trends and strategic shifts in space.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, emphasizing its focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The funding signals a strong pull from the Department of Defense, which is increasingly prioritizing space security. With a valuation of $1.6 billion, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the defense sector.
stories.soWhat: In a space sector where cash flow is king, True Anomaly's funding highlights the growing urgency for co-orbital security solutions.

stories.head: SES and Eutelsat cancel GEO expansion satellites
stories.body: SES has joined Eutelsat in scrapping plans for GEO expansion satellites, a move that reflects the shifting dynamics in satellite communications. This decision comes as both companies reassess their strategies amid mounting competition and changing market demands. As a result, stakeholders are left wondering where the growth will come from in an increasingly crowded satellite landscape.
stories.soWhat: When even established players are hitting the brakes, it suggests the GEO market may be more fragile than previously thought.

stories.head: SpaceX sets date for Starship version 3 launch
stories.body: SpaceX has announced a launch date for its much-anticipated Starship version 3, a critical component for NASA's lunar ambitions. This launch is expected to take place in the coming weeks, as SpaceX aims to solidify its position as the go-to launch provider for lunar missions. However, with previous delays fresh in everyone's mind, skepticism remains about whether this date will hold.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX can actually launch on time, it might just silence some of the critics—at least temporarily.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on lunar navigation systems
watchlist.body: Northrop Grumman's entry into the lunar navigation market could reshape how future missions are conducted.

watchlist.title: Defense-tech IPO window remains open
watchlist.body: With the recent buzz around defense-tech IPOs, companies like Anduril may soon be looking to capitalize.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: After a hefty funding round, True Anomaly's strategy for co-orbital security will be closely watched.

watchlist.title: SES and Eutelsat's next steps
watchlist.body: The cancellation of GEO satellites raises questions about SES and Eutelsat's future strategies in satellite communications.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
